headline: FOUNDERS METALS HITS 27M AT 20.38 G/T GOLD IN STEP-OUT WEST ZONE — NEW DISTRICT TARGET OPENS AT ANTINO, SURINAME
snippet: Founders Metals Inc. (TSXV: FDR) reported that the first step-out hole at the newly identified Upper Antino-West Zone — 1.2 km west of the established Froyo Zone — returned 27.0m at 20.38 g/t gold from 100.0m depth, including a 10.0m sub-interval at 43.26 g/t Au. The zone is open and five follow-up holes are complete with drilling ongoing. Company CEO called FR251 'one of the best single intercepts in Antino's history,' and the West Zone is now the top 2026 drill priority.

headline: COPPER SMASHES ALL-TIME HIGH AT $14,703/T ON LME — TARIFF SPECULATION DRAINS WAREHOUSES 40% IN THREE MONTHS
snippet: Three-month LME copper touched a new all-time high of $14,703 a metric ton on September 9, 2026, pushed higher by a flood of metal moving to US warehouses ahead of anticipated tariffs on refined copper imports. LME stocks have shed nearly 40% since late May; SHFE inventories are down 85% from a mid-March peak. Chile and Peru face permitting delays and storm-related disruptions, removing any near-term supply relief from the two largest-producing nations.

headline: STANMORE RESOURCES BAGS 724M-TONNE MORANBAH SOUTH COKING COAL BLOCK FOR US$105M — EXXARO FLIPS ANGLO STAKE IN DAYS
snippet: Stanmore Resources (ASX: SMR) agreed to acquire 100% of the Moranbah South metallurgical coal tenements in Queensland's Bowen Basin from Exxaro Resources for US$105 million, funded entirely from existing cash. The block sits directly adjacent to Stanmore's Eagle Downs and Isaac Downs Extension projects and holds 724 million tonnes of measured and indicated Goonyella Middle Seam coking coal — premium hard coking coal quality. Exxaro bought Anglo American's 50% JV stake and immediately sold the combined 100% interest to Stanmore, closing the deal within days.

headline: URANIUM NEAR $90/LB AS CAMECO AND KAZATOMPROM BOTH CUT GUIDANCE — SUPPLY DEFICIT STRUCTURALLY WIDER HEADING INTO WINTER
snippet: Uranium spot rose to $89.65/lb on September 8, hovering near a six-month high of $90.60 touched on August 26. Cameco's McArthur River has trimmed production guidance after Orano's McClean Lake mill suffered a sulfuric acid plant failure in late June, temporarily shuttering Cigar Lake — the world's highest-grade operating uranium mine. Kazatomprom also cut 2026 output by roughly 10%, citing sulfuric acid supply constraints at its TQZ plant. The dual guidance reductions have structurally widened the supply deficit, supporting the case for utilities to lock in longer-term supply contracts.

headline: PUREPOINT AND ISOENERGY JV APPROVES 2026 DRILL PROGRAM TO ADVANCE NOVA URANIUM DISCOVERY AT DORADO PROJECT
snippet: The PurePoint Uranium (TSXV: PTU) and IsoEnergy (TSX: ISO) joint venture has approved a 2026 exploration program targeting the Nova discovery at the Dorado Project in the Athabasca Basin. The Nova discovery — originally intersected in 2025 — sits in one of the world's most prolific uranium districts, and the 2026 program is designed to test extensions and refine the geometry of the basement-hosted mineralization ahead of a resource estimate.

headline: USA RARE EARTH STOCK DOWN 60% FROM SPAC PEAK — IS SEPTEMBER THE ENTRY POINT FOR THIS STILL-LOSS-MAKING STARTUP?
snippet: USA Rare Earth (NASDAQ: UREE), which went public via SPAC merger in March 2026, has fallen roughly 60% from its post-listing peak to around $17.66/share as investors reassess the timeline and capital requirements to build out domestic rare earth processing capacity. Motley Fool's September 9 analysis examines whether the selloff has created a genuine entry point or reflects execution risk at a company still years from producing commercial quantities of critical NdPr magnet material.

headline: CHINA RARE EARTH EXPORT CONTROL SUSPENSION EXPIRES NOVEMBER 10 — THE SINGLE CLEAREST SECTOR CATALYST LEFT ON THE CALENDAR
snippet: China's suspended rare earth export controls are set to expire on November 10, 2026 — the most clearly defined single catalyst now in sight for the rare earth sector. September's basket moved a muted +0.31% on average; germanium led at +10.04% while scandium fell 7.36%. The November 10 date has sharpened attention from downstream users in EV motors, wind turbines, and defense electronics, all of which depend on NdPr and other magnet materials with few viable short-term substitutes outside Chinese supply chains.

headline: CHINA LITHIUM BATTERY CONSUMPTION TAX HITS SEPT 1 — FIVE MAJOR MANUFACTURERS RAISE PRICES 2–10% WITHIN THE FIRST WEEK
snippet: A reinstated 2% consumption tax on lithium-ion batteries and battery materials took effect in China on September 1, ending a decade-long exemption. Within days, at least five major energy storage and battery producers issued price-hike notices ranging from 2% to 10%, passing the cost increase downstream to EV makers and grid storage buyers. Combined with Beijing's phased elimination of VAT export rebates (from 9% to 6% in April 2026, then to zero by January 2027), the policy shift is structurally raising the floor price of Chinese-produced lithium cells for global buyers.

headline: GDX AT RECORD MARGINS BUT DOWN FROM HIGHS — ANALYSTS SEE 3X GOLD LEVERAGE FOR PATIENT BUYERS AT CURRENT ENTRY
snippet: Gold miners (GDX) returned 108% year-over-year through April 2026, but have since pulled back 20% from highs as the September Fed-hike narrative pressures the gold price. Analysts note that the underlying margin picture remains exceptional: with gold near $4,400 and all-in sustaining costs still tracking $1,400–$1,600 for major producers, free cash flow yields are at record levels. Historical GDX-to-gold leverage of 2x–3x on upswings means a move back toward $4,500–$4,600 gold could drive outsized equity gains for producers and juniors alike.

headline: SILVER AT $66 AS SIXTH CONSECUTIVE ANNUAL SUPPLY DEFICIT DEEPENS TO 46M OZ — SOLAR THRIFTING PARTIALLY OFFSETS INDUSTRIAL DEMAND
snippet: Silver trades near $66/oz ahead of this week's US inflation data as the 2026 market tracks toward its sixth consecutive annual supply deficit, with the shortfall estimated at 46.3 million ounces. Solar panel manufacturers have responded to higher silver prices with substitution and thrifting, trimming industrial demand by an estimated 3% year-over-year, but the structural deficit from the broader electrification complex — EVs, grid storage, AI data centers — continues to underpin the long-term supply case alongside monetary demand returning to the metal.
